title: Manganese (Mn): Element, Uses and Formula
summary: This alloying element has many benefits that extend far beyond steelmaking.
body_text: 1. Manganese for Removing Oxygen (Deoxidizer) Manganese serves as a primary deoxidizer in steelmaking by reacting chemically with dissolved oxygen in molten steel before the metal solidifies. Oxygen dissolves in liquid steel during melting and refining operations, reaching concentrations of 300 ppm to 600 ppm in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) steel at tapping temperatures near 1,600°C. At these temperatures, manganese reacts with dissolved oxygen according to the reaction Mn + O → MnO, forming solid manganese oxide inclusions that are lighter than liquid steel and float upward into the slag layer for removal. The deoxidation efficiency of manganese depends on both its concentration and the bath temperature, with higher manganese additions producing lower residual oxygen levels in the final steel. A manganese addition of 0.30% reduces dissolved oxygen from approximately 500 ppm to 100 ppm in low-carbon steel. Aluminum and silicon are added alongside manganese in killed steel production to achieve oxygen levels below 20 ppm for applications requiring maximum cleanliness and homogeneity. 2. Manganese for Removing Impurities Manganese contributes to impurity removal during steelmaking by reacting with dissolved elements and transferring them into the slag phase, reducing their harmful concentration in the solidified steel. Phosphorus and sulfur represent the two most damaging impurities in steel, as phosphorus promotes cold brittleness and sulfur causes hot shortness during hot working processes. Manganese binds sulfur preferentially, forming MnS inclusions rather than allowing the formation of iron sulfide (FeS) films at grain boundaries. The relative affinity of manganese for sulfur is approximately 10 times greater than that of iron at steelmaking temperatures, ensuring sulfur reports to the inclusion phase rather than remaining in solid solution. Manganese additions during secondary metallurgy (ladle refining) produce inclusion morphology control, where sulfide inclusion shape affects machinability and fatigue performance in the final product. Globular MnS inclusions formed at manganese-to-sulfur ratios above 10:1 improve machinability without significantly reducing transverse toughness in bar and plate steel products. 3. Manganese for Controlling Sulfur Manganese controls sulfur in steel by combining with dissolved sulfur atoms to form manganese sulfide (MnS) inclusions, preventing the formation of damaging iron sulfide phases. Iron sulfide (FeS) forms a low-melting eutectic with iron at approximately 985°C, creating liquid films at austenite grain boundaries during hot rolling operations. The liquid grain boundary films rupture under rolling pressure, producing surface cracks and internal tears called hot shortness, which ruins the surface quality and mechanical integrity of hot-worked products. Manganese sulfide forms at a higher melting point than FeS and solidifies as discrete globular inclusions distributed uniformly through the steel matrix, eliminating the grain boundary film problem entirely. A minimum manganese-to-sulfur ratio of 8:1 by weight is required to fully suppress FeS formation, with ratios of 20:1 to 40:1 specified in high-quality steel grades. Free-machining steels intentionally maintain higher sulfur levels (0.15% to 0.35% S) paired with elevated manganese (0.60% to 1.65% Mn) to produce controlled MnS inclusions that act as chip-breaking agents during high-speed machining operations. 4. Manganese for Preventing Brittleness Manganese prevents brittleness in steel by eliminating the grain boundary iron sulfide films and dissolved sulfur concentrations that promote intergranular fracture under impact and low-temperature loading. Brittleness in steel manifests as a sudden loss of toughness, causing fracture at stress levels well below the material's tensile strength without significant plastic deformation. Iron sulfide concentrations at grain boundaries reduce grain boundary cohesion, lowering the energy required to initiate and propagate cracks along grain boundaries rather than through the stronger grain interiors. Manganese removes sulfur from solid solution by forming MnS inclusions, restoring grain boundary cohesion and allowing the material to absorb impact energy through plastic deformation rather than brittle fracture. Ductile-to-brittle transition temperature (DBTT) testing confirms that manganese-alloyed steels shift their transition temperature downward by 5°C to 10°C per 0.1% Mn addition in low-carbon structural steel grades. Steels destined for arctic pipeline and offshore structural applications specify minimum manganese contents of 1.0% to 1.6% to guarantee adequate toughness at service temperatures reaching -60°C. 5. Manganese for Increasing Strength Manganese increases strength in steel through solid solution hardening, a mechanism where manganese atoms substitute for iron atoms in the crystal lattice and create localized lattice distortions that impede dislocation movement. Dislocations are the primary carriers of plastic deformation in metallic crystals, and obstacles to dislocation motion directly increase the stress required to deform the material. Each 0.10% increase in manganese content raises the yield strength of low-carbon steel by approximately 3 MPa to 5 MPa and tensile strength by 10 MPa to 15 MPa through the solid solution strengthening mechanism alone. Combined with controlled carbon content and thermomechanical processing, manganese enables high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steels to achieve yield strengths from 345 MPa to 690 MPa using total alloy additions below 2% by weight. Grade 50 structural steel (ASTM A572) achieves a minimum yield strength of 345 MPa using carbon content below 0.23% paired with manganese contents up to 1.35%, demonstrating the strength contribution of manganese without excessive carbon that would reduce weldability. 6. Manganese for Increasing Hardness Manganese increases hardness in steel by enhancing hardenability, the ability of a steel to form hard martensitic and bainitic microstructures during quenching from austenitizing temperatures. Martensite is the hardest microstructural phase achievable in steel through heat treatment, and its formation depends on cooling the steel faster than the critical cooling rate defined by the CCT diagram. Manganese lowers the critical cooling rate by stabilizing austenite during cooling, allowing martensite formation at slower quench rates and through greater section thicknesses. A 1.0% manganese addition reduces the critical cooling rate by approximately 30% compared to equivalent carbon steel, enabling through-hardening of sections up to 50 mm thick with water quenching or 25 mm thick with oil quenching. Surface hardness values achievable in manganese-alloyed tool steels reach 58 HRC to 62 HRC after quench and temper heat treatment, compared to 45 HRC to 50 HRC in equivalent plain carbon steels without manganese additions at matching carbon levels. 7. Manganese for Improving Wear Resistance Manganese improves wear resistance in steel through two distinct mechanisms depending on the alloy's manganese concentration. At standard concentrations from 0.6% to 1.8%, manganese enhances hardness and hardenability, producing harder tempered martensite microstructures that resist abrasive wear in tools, gears, and cutting components. Manganese produces Hadfield austenitic manganese steel at high concentrations from 11% to 14%, which demonstrates exceptional work-hardening behavior under impact and compressive contact loading. Hadfield steel begins service with a relatively low hardness of 170 HBW to 220 HBW in the solution-annealed condition, but repeated impact loading progressively work-hardens the surface to 450 HBW to 550 HBW as dislocation density and strain-induced martensite accumulate near the contact surface. The wear rate of Hadfield steel under combined impact and abrasion loading is 3 to 10 times lower than that of standard hardened steel in equivalent service conditions. Railroad crossings, rock crusher jaws, cement mill liners, and dragline bucket lips represent the primary applications exploiting the superior wear resistance of high-manganese steel. 8. Manganese for Improving Hardenability Manganese improves hardenability by stabilizing austenite during cooling and reducing the critical cooling rate needed to suppress the formation of softer ferritic and pearlitic microstructures. Hardenability is measured through the Jominy end-quench test, which subjects a standard cylindrical specimen to water quenching at one end and measures hardness at defined distances from the quenched face. Greater hardenability produces measurable hardness values farther from the quenched end, confirming deeper martensitic transformation through the section. Manganese is among the most cost-effective hardenability-improving elements, with a hardenability multiplying factor of 3.3 per 1.0% Mn addition, compared to 3.5 for chromium and 4.0 for molybdenum. SAE/AISI H-steels (H-band steels) with guaranteed hardenability ranges specify minimum manganese contents of 0.75% to 1.00% to meet Jominy hardness requirements for automotive gear, axle, and crankshaft applications. Deeper hardenability reduces distortion risk during quenching of large cross-sections by enabling slower quench media (oil or air) rather than aggressive water quenching. 9. Manganese for Enhancing Toughness Manganese enhances toughness in steel by refining austenite grain size during hot rolling, promoting grain boundary pinning that limits grain growth at elevated temperatures. Smaller grain sizes increase the total grain boundary area per unit volume, creating more obstacles to crack propagation and raising the energy absorbed per unit area of fracture surface. The Hall-Petch relationship quantifies the grain size effect, showing that reducing the average grain diameter from 100 μm to 20 μm increases yield strength by approximately 80 MPa and simultaneously improves toughness. Manganese additions from 1.0% to 1.6% in normalized structural steels achieve average prior austenite grain sizes of 20 μm to 40 μm after hot rolling, compared to 60 μm to 100 μm in equivalent plain carbon steels processed identically. Charpy V-notch impact values at -20°C reach 80 J to 120 J in manganese-alloyed structural steels versus 20 J to 40 J in plain carbon steels of equivalent strength, demonstrating the measurable toughness enhancement manganese provides for structural and pressure vessel applications operating in cold service environments. 10. Manganese for Stabilizing Austenite Structure Manganese stabilizes the austenite crystal structure in steel by lowering the martensite start (Ms) temperature and expanding the austenite phase field on the iron-carbon phase diagram. Austenite (FCC iron) is stable above 723°C in plain carbon steel and transforms to ferrite, pearlite, or martensite on cooling, depending on cooling rate and composition. Manganese is an austenite-stabilizing element with a coefficient that lowers the Ms temperature by approximately 30°C to 45°C per 1.0% Mn addition, retaining austenite at progressively lower temperatures as manganese content increases. Manganese stabilizes austenite completely at room temperature at concentrations above 12%, producing fully austenitic steel without any heat treatment requirement. AISI 200-series austenitic stainless steels (AISI 201, 202) use manganese contents from 5.5% to 10.0% to stabilize the FCC structure as a partial substitute for nickel, reducing alloy cost by 40% to 60% compared to AISI 300-series grades. The retained austenite in these alloys provides non-magnetic behavior, excellent formability, and corrosion resistance suitable for food processing equipment, kitchen utensils, and architectural cladding applications. How Can Manganese Be Used as a 3D Printing Material? Manganese has not yet been widely used as a 3D printing material compared to other metals like titanium, aluminum, and steel. However, there are ongoing research and development efforts exploring the potential use of manganese in 3D printing applications. One of the main challenges with using manganese in 3D printing is its high vapor pressure, which makes it difficult to print using traditional 3D printing methods like FDM or SLS. However, new techniques like binder jetting and PBF have shown promising results in printing high-melting-point metals like manganese. Manganese, as an alloying element, has several properties that make it an attractive material for 3D printing, including its high strength and hardness. Manganese additions can support lightweighting in structural alloys and provide good thermal conductivity, making it suitable for various applications in industries like aerospace, automotive, and electronics. What Is the Role of Manganese in 3D Printing? Manganese is not used for 3D printing in its pure form, but could potentially play a role as an alloying element in raw 3D printing materials for some applications. Here are a few possible roles that manganese could play in 3D printing: Strengthening Alloys : Manganese is often used as an alloying element in steel, aluminum, and other metals to improve their strength, toughness, and corrosion resistance. By adding small amounts of manganese to 3D printing materials, it could be possible to produce parts with improved mechanical properties. Lightweighting : Manganese-aluminum alloys are lightweight and have good strength-to-weight ratios. These alloys could be used to produce lightweight parts for the aerospace and automotive industries. It could be possible to further reduce the weight of these parts without sacrificing strength by using 3D printing to produce complex geometries. Thermal Management : Manganese has high thermal conductivity, which makes it useful for creating parts that require effective thermal management. For example, 3D-printed heat exchangers or other thermal management components may benefit from the use of manganese or manganese alloys. How Is the Quality of a Manganese 3D Printed Material? Granted, manganese hasn’t yet joined the ranks of titanium, aluminum, and steel when it comes to 3D printing, but a lot of research and development efforts are going into making it happen. The first step will likely be to make it an alloying element in another 3D printing material. Just like it does when combined with metals for other applications, manganese can be used in 3D printing to make strong, lightweight, and thermal-resistant parts for aerospace, automotive, electronics, and beyond. The process can much more easily make products with complex shapes, and its thermal management could be useful for things like heat exchangers. How Does the Availability of Manganese Impact Its Use in 3D Printing? The availability of manganese can impact its use in 3D printing because the cost and accessibility of the material can affect its adoption and commercial viability. If manganese is widely available and affordable, it can be used more easily in 3D printing applications. However, if there are shortages or limited availability, the cost of manganese may increase, making it less competitive with other 3D printing materials. In addition, limited availability may lead to challenges in maintaining consistent quality and quantity of manganese for 3D printing. Although the availability of manganese is a factor that can impact its use in 3D printing, it is not the only consideration. The suitability of the material for a particular application, its mechanical properties, and the cost of production are all important factors that must be taken into account when considering manganese as a 3D printing material. Why Is Manganese Added to Structural Steel Grades? Manganese is added to structural steel grades to increase yield strength, tensile strength, and toughness while maintaining adequate weldability and formability for construction applications. Structural steel grades without manganese rely entirely on carbon for strengthening, but carbon additions above 0.30% significantly reduce weldability and increase cold cracking susceptibility. Manganese provides a more favorable strengthening mechanism through solid solution hardening and hardenability enhancement, achieving target strength levels at lower carbon equivalents. ASTM A529 Grade 50 structural steel specifies a minimum yield strength of 345 MPa using a carbon content capped at 0.27% paired with manganese content up to 1.35%, demonstrating the strength contribution of manganese at reduced carbon levels. ASTM A572 Grade 65 achieves a minimum yield strength of 450 MPa through controlled manganese additions up to 1.65%. The combination of increased strength, impact resistance, and retained weldability from manganese alloying makes it the preferred strengthening agent in wide-flange beams, columns, and plate girders used across bridge and building construction, detailed in Steel Grades . Does Manganese Improve Strength in Alloy Steel? Manganese improves strength in alloy steel through solid solution hardening and hardenability enhancement, producing measurable increases in yield strength, tensile strength, and fatigue resistance. In alloy steels, manganese acts synergistically with carbon, chromium, molybdenum, and nickel to achieve strength levels far above what any single element produces alone. SAE 1340 manganese alloy steel contains 1.60% to 1.90% Mn and achieves a tensile strength of 1,000 MPa to 1,200 MPa after quench and temper heat treatment, compared to 600 MPa to 700 MPa in plain carbon steel of equivalent carbon content. Medium-carbon manganese alloy steels are widely specified for automotive axle shafts, transmission gears, and suspension springs where high strength combined with toughness is required throughout a service life of hundreds of thousands of loading cycles. The strength improvements manganese delivers in alloy steel make it one of the most cost-effective alloying elements available to the steel industry. How Is Manganese Sourced for Industrial Production? Manganese for industrial production is sourced through the mining of manganese-bearing ore deposits, primarily from oxide, carbonate, and silicate mineral formations distributed across major deposits in South Africa, Australia, Gabon, Brazil, and China. South Africa holds approximately 80% of the world's known manganese resources, primarily in the Kalahari Manganese Field in the Northern Cape Province. Global manganese ore production reaches approximately 20 million metric tons per year, with the majority processed into ferromanganese and silicomanganese alloys used directly in steelmaking. Mined ore undergoes crushing, screening, and beneficiation to concentrate manganese content from run-of-mine grades of 25% to 40% Mn up to commercial grades of 44% to 48% Mn. Hydrometallurgical and pyrometallurgical refining processes convert ore concentrates into ferroalloys (FeMn, SiMn) for direct steelmaking additions or into electrolytic manganese metal (EMM) with purity above 99.7% for specialty alloy and battery applications. Transportation infrastructure connecting mines to coastal ports is a critical factor in the manganese supply chain reliability, as the Kalahari field relies on a dedicated rail corridor to Saldanha Bay for export to global steel mills. What Types of Manganese Ore Are Used in Engineering Supply Chains? The types of Manganese Ore that are used in engineering supply chains are listed below. Pyrolusite (MnO₂) : Pyrolusite is the most abundant and economically significant manganese ore, containing up to 63% Mn by weight in its pure form. It serves as the primary feedstock for producing electrolytic manganese dioxide (EMD) used in dry-cell batteries and as a direct charge material in electric arc furnace ferroalloy production. Romanechite (BaMn₉O₁₈·2H₂O) : Romanechite is a mixed barium-manganese oxide ore found in secondary oxidation zones of manganese deposits. It contributes to the overall manganese content of oxide ore blends processed in ferromanganese smelters and contains 45% to 55% Mn in high-grade specimens. Rhodochrosite (MnCO₃) : Rhodochrosite is a manganese carbonate mineral containing approximately 47.8% Mn in its pure form. Carbonate ores require calcination before smelting to decompose the carbonate and release CO₂, adding processing cost but producing a clean, low-phosphorus manganese feed for high-purity alloy production. Manganite (MnO(OH)) : Manganite is a manganese oxyhydroxide mineral containing approximately 62% Mn, found in hydrothermal and secondary oxidation environments. It is processed alongside pyrolusite in ore blends destined for ferroalloy smelting and chemical-grade manganese compound production. Is Manganese Extracted Primarily From Oxide Minerals? Manganese is extracted primarily from oxide minerals, with pyrolusite (MnO₂) and romanechite accounting for the majority of global manganese ore production by tonnage. Oxide manganese ores dominate commercial deposits because oxidative weathering of primary manganese silicates and carbonates concentrates manganese into near-surface oxide layers over geological time, making them accessible for open-cut and shallow underground mining. The Kalahari Manganese Field in South Africa, the world's largest manganese deposit, consists predominantly of oxide ores developed through supergene enrichment of underlying carbonate ore bodies, with the Wessels and Hotazel mines extracting pyrolusite and romanechite at grades exceeding 48% Mn. Carbonate ores (rhodochrosite) and silicate ores (rhodonite) exist in significant quantities but require more energy-intensive processing, limiting their economic attractiveness relative to oxide ores. Seafloor polymetallic nodules represent a future potential source of manganese oxide minerals from deep ocean environments, containing 15% to 30% Mn alongside copper, nickel, and cobalt. How Does Manganese Influence the Performance of Iron Based Alloys? Manganese influences the performance of iron-based alloys by improving strength, hardness, toughness, and wear resistance through metallurgical mechanisms that operate at the atomic and microstructural levels. Manganese dissolves into the iron lattice as a substitutional solid solution element in iron-based alloys, creating lattice strain that impedes dislocation movement and raises the material's resistance to plastic deformation. The effect is measurable across a wide composition range, from 0.25% Mn in plain carbon steels to 14% Mn in Hadfield austenitic manganese steels. Manganese alters the phase transformation behavior of iron-based alloys by stabilizing austenite, lowering transformation temperatures, and increasing hardenability during heat treatment. The combination of solid solution strengthening, transformation control, and grain refinement effects makes manganese a uniquely versatile alloying element capable of improving multiple properties simultaneously without requiring complex heat treatment schedules. Gray cast iron, ductile iron, and white iron all benefit from controlled manganese additions, with 0.5% to 0.8% Mn used in gray iron to neutralize sulfur and prevent brittleness while improving tensile strength from 150 MPa to 250 MPa in standard grades. How Does Manganese Modify the Properties of Carbon Steel? Manganese modifies the properties of carbon steel by increasing yield strength, tensile strength, hardenability, and impact toughness while simultaneously reducing the harmful effects of dissolved sulfur on hot workability. In plain carbon steel, manganese content ranging from 0.30% to 0.90% raises yield strength by 20 MPa to 60 MPa through solid solution hardening without requiring heat treatment beyond normalizing or hot rolling. Higher manganese contents from 1.0% to 1.65% in medium-carbon steels produce significant hardenability improvements, enabling through-hardening of sections up to 75 mm in diameter with oil quenching. The interaction of manganese with carbon produces the greatest strengthening effect, as both elements together shift the eutectoid point composition and promote finer pearlite spacing during transformation. AISI 1045 carbon steel achieves a tensile strength of 570 MPa in the hot-rolled condition, while AISI 1345 (equivalent carbon with 1.60% to 1.90% Mn) achieves 650 MPa in the same processing condition. Manganese also lowers the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature in carbon steel by approximately 5.5°C per 0.1% Mn addition, qualifying higher-manganese carbon steels for use in carbon steel applications exposed to sub-zero service temperatures. Is Manganese Harder Than Pure Iron in Metallic Form? Manganese is harder than pure iron in metallic form, with alpha manganese (α-Mn) exhibiting a Vickers hardness of approximately 196 HV compared to pure iron at 70 HV to 80 HV in the annealed condition. The hardness difference stems from the complex crystal structure of alpha manganese, which contains 58 atoms per unit cell in a cubic arrangement with multiple non-equivalent atomic sites, creating significant internal lattice strain that resists plastic deformation. Pure iron adopts a simple body-centered cubic (BCC) structure with 2 atoms per unit cell and low intrinsic hardness due to the ease of dislocation movement through the regular lattice. Despite being harder than iron individually, pure manganese is brittle and not practically usable as a structural metal without alloying. The hardness of manganese translates into practical benefit primarily through alloying, where dissolved manganese atoms in the iron lattice contribute their lattice distortion effects to measurably increase the hardness of the resulting alloy above that of pure iron alone. How Do Different Steel Grades Use Manganese for Specific Applications? Different steel grades use manganese at varying concentrations to achieve the mechanical properties required for each specific application, with higher manganese levels targeting strength, wear resistance, and hardenability, while lower levels focus on weldability and formability. Low-carbon structural steels (ASTM A36, A572) use manganese from 0.80% to 1.65% to achieve yield strengths from 250 MPa to 450 MPa while maintaining carbon equivalent values low enough for field welding without preheat. Medium-carbon alloy steels (SAE 1340, 4140) use manganese from 0.75% to 1.90% to achieve through-hardened tensile strengths above 1,000 MPa for automotive and machinery components. Rail steel grades specify manganese from 0.70% to 1.10% to balance wear resistance at the rail head with toughness in the web and base. Wear-resistant plate grades (AR400, AR500) use manganese from 0.90% to 1.50% paired with boron additions to achieve surface hardness from 400 HBW to 500 HBW for mining and material handling equipment. The customization of manganese content across different steel grades enables engineers to tailor mechanical performance precisely to application requirements without changing alloy families or processing routes. What Is the Purpose of Manganese in Structural Steel Like A529? The purpose of manganese in structural steel like A529 is to provide the strength and toughness required for load-bearing structural applications while maintaining the weldability necessary for field fabrication and connection work. ASTM A529 covers carbon-manganese structural steel in shapes and plates, with Grade 50 specifying a minimum yield strength of 345 MPa and minimum tensile strength of 485 MPa. The specification permits manganese contents up to 1.35% by weight, paired with a maximum carbon content of 0.27%, to achieve the target mechanical properties at a carbon equivalent value compatible with standard welding procedures. Manganese contributes to the fatigue resistance of A529 structural members subjected to dynamic loading from wind, traffic, and mechanical equipment. The toughness enhancement from manganese refinement of austenite grain size ensures adequate Charpy impact values for connections in earthquake-resistant structures and transportation infrastructure. Engineers specify A529 carbon steel with controlled manganese content for column base plates, beam webs, and gusset plates in structures where the combination of strength, weldability, and toughness detailed in A529 Carbon Steel specifications governs material selection. Does Manganese Improve Weldability and Durability? Manganese improves weldability and durability in steel through complementary metallurgical effects that operate during welding and long-term service loading. Weldability improves because manganese allows target strength levels to be achieved at lower carbon contents, reducing the carbon equivalent (CE) value that governs preheat requirements and cold cracking susceptibility. The International Institute of Welding (IIW) carbon equivalent formula CE = C + Mn/6 + (Cr+Mo+V)/5 + (Ni+Cu)/15 directly quantifies manganese's contribution, where 1.0% Mn contributes 0.17 to the total carbon equivalent. Durability improves because manganese increases toughness, wear resistance, and fatigue life simultaneously. Structural members with higher manganese content maintain integrity under cyclic loading over 10⁷ to 10⁸ loading cycles in fatigue-critical applications like bridges and crane girders. Corrosion-resistant weathering steel grades (ASTM A588) use controlled manganese additions alongside copper and chromium to achieve a 4-to-8 times longer service life than plain carbon steel in atmospheric exposure conditions. What Are the Safety Considerations When Handling Manganese in Industry? The safety considerations when handling Manganese in industry are listed below. Inhalation Hazard (Manganese Dust and Fume) : Exposure to manganese dust and fume above the OSHA permissible exposure limit (PEL) of 5 mg/m³ as a ceiling value causes manganism, a neurological disorder with symptoms resembling Parkinson's disease. Welding on manganese-containing steel produces manganese fume concentrations that require local exhaust ventilation and respiratory protection using P100 or supplied-air respirators in enclosed spaces. Dermal and Eye Contact : Manganese dust and manganese compound solutions cause skin and eye irritation upon direct contact. Appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including chemical-resistant gloves, safety goggles, and face shields, is required when handling manganese ore, ferromanganese alloys, or manganese compound solutions in industrial processing environments. Fire and Explosion Risk (Manganese Powder) : Fine manganese powder with particle sizes below 44 μm presents a dust explosion hazard when suspended in air at concentrations above the minimum explosive concentration (MEC) of approximately 210 g/m³. Processing areas handling manganese powder require explosion-proof electrical equipment, grounding systems, and dust suppression measures per NFPA 654 combustible dust safety standards. Environmental Contamination : Manganese ore processing generates tailings and wastewater containing dissolved Mn²⁺ ions at concentrations requiring treatment before discharge. The EPA secondary drinking water standard limits manganese in drinking water to 0.05 mg/L (50 ppb) due to aesthetic concerns at higher concentrations. Industrial sites must implement containment, water treatment, and monitoring systems to prevent manganese contamination of surface water and groundwater resources near processing facilities. Chronic Neurological Exposure Risk : Long-term occupational exposure to airborne manganese at concentrations above 0.1 mg/m³ produces cumulative neurological damage even without acute poisoning symptoms. Medical surveillance programs, including baseline and periodic neurological assessments, are required for workers in ferroalloy smelting, welding, and battery manufacturing, where sustained manganese exposure occurs throughout extended employment periods.

title: Privacy-Preserving Prompt Tuning for Large Language Model Services
summary: Tutorials, guides and deep dives into the best techniques and research for building reliable AI.
body_text: Do not index Original Paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06212 Blog URL blog.athina.ai /privacy...services Original Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.06212 By: Yansong Li , Zhixing Tan , Yang Liu Abstract: Prompt tuning provides an efficient way for users to customize Large Language Models (LLMs) with their private data in the emerging LLM service scenario. However, the sensitive nature of private data brings the need for privacy preservation in LLM service customization. Based on prompt tuning, we propose Privacy-Preserving Prompt Tuning (RAPT), a framework that provides privacy guarantees for LLM services. \textsc{rapt} adopts a local privacy setting, allowing users to privatize their data locally with local differential privacy. As prompt tuning performs poorly when directly trained on privatized data, we introduce a novel privatized token reconstruction task that is trained jointly with the downstream task, allowing LLMs to learn better task-dependent representations. Despite the simplicity of our framework, experiments show that RAPT achieves competitive performance across tasks while providing privacy guarantees against adversaries. Summary Notes Keeping Data Private in AI with RAPT The world of artificial intelligence (AI) is always growing, with large language models (LLMs) leading the way. These models are great at understanding and creating text that sounds human. A common way to make these models do specific tasks is through prompt tuning, which adjusts the models with little extra training. However, when businesses use cloud services for prompt tuning, they worry about keeping their sensitive data private. This blog introduces an innovative solution called RAPT that protects data privacy without losing the benefits of LLMs. Introduction to RAPT: A New Hope for Data Privacy RAPT, short for Privacy-Preserving Prompt Tuning, is a new tool designed to keep sensitive information safe while still making the most out of LLMs. It uses a smart technique called local differential privacy in the prompt tuning process, making sure that sensitive data stays confidential. Inside the RAPT Framework Local Privacy Approach : With RAPT, users can make their data private on their own devices by adding a bit of noise to it. This ensures the data remains private even when used to train LLMs. Making Tokens Private Again : To avoid losing performance with the added privacy, RAPT introduces a way to teach the LLM to guess the original content from its noisier version, helping it understand better. How RAPT Works Using RAPT involves a few steps: Making Data Private : Users first make their data private with differential privacy before sending it to the cloud. Tuning LLMs with RAPT : Then, they use the cloud-based LLMs' prompt tuning services with this private data. Reconstructing Private Tokens : The LLM tries to guess the original data from its private version, improving its performance. Tests on models like BERT and T5, for tasks such as understanding emotions in text, show that RAPT is effective at protecting privacy without sacrificing quality. Other Methods Research into keeping LLMs private has looked at centralized methods, which rely on the cloud provider, and local methods, which keep more control with the user. RAPT offers a middle ground, providing strong privacy without depending on the provider. Results RAPT does a better job at protecting privacy compared to traditional prompt tuning, without losing much in performance. It works well for different AI tasks and models, making it a big step forward for the field. Conclusion RAPT meets the critical need for privacy in using LLMs for personalized tasks. By combining local differential privacy with a technique to guess original content from its private form, it allows the safe use of cloud-based LLM services without risking sensitive data. Future research could expand this approach to more models and types of privacy threats. Keywords: Large Language Models, Privacy-Preserving, Prompt Tuning, Differential Privacy, Natural Language Processing. RAPT represents a significant advancement in responsible AI development, offering a way for businesses to use cutting-edge technology while protecting sensitive information. This approach not only enhances security in AI deployments but also sets new standards for responsible AI in our data-centric world. title: Guia Completo da Telefonia Móvel para Empresas no Brasil
summary: A telefonia móvel para empresas é um dos pilares da comunicação empresarial. Neste artigo, vamos explorar um guia completo sobre o assunto.
body_text: Olá! Seja bem-vindo ao guia completo da telefonia móvel para empresas no Brasil, elaborado com carinho pela equipe Salvy. Sabemos que o mundo dos negócios está sempre em constante evolução e a comunicação é um pilar fundamental para o sucesso de qualquer empresa. Por isso, preparamos este guia para ajudá-lo a navegar pelas águas da telefonia móvel com segurança e praticidade. Vamos nessa? A importância da telefonia móvel para empresas no Brasil A telefonia móvel é, sem dúvida, uma ferramenta indispensável no cenário empresarial brasileiro. Ela permite uma comunicação rápida e eficiente entre colaboradores, fornecedores e clientes, além de proporcionar acesso a informações e recursos importantes para o desempenho das atividades corporativas. Afinal, quem não gosta de resolver problemas e fechar negócios com apenas alguns toques na tela do smartphone? As empresas que investem em soluções de telefonia móvel estão sempre à frente, garantindo agilidade e competitividade no mercado. Por isso, é essencial que você entenda tudo sobre esse universo e saiba como aplicá-lo na sua empresa. Visão geral do mercado de telefonia móvel no Brasil O Brasil é um dos maiores mercados de telefonia móvel do mundo, com milhões de usuários e um alto índice de penetração de smartphones. Isso significa que as empresas precisam estar atentas às tendências e inovações do setor para não ficarem para trás. Existem diversas operadoras de telefonia móvel no país, oferecendo uma ampla variedade de planos e serviços para atender às diferentes necessidades das empresas. Além disso, a evolução tecnológica tem sido constante, com a chegada das redes 5G e a popularização de dispositivos com múltiplas funcionalidades, como smartphones e tablets. Aqui na Salvy, acreditamos que é fundamental que as empresas estejam bem informadas para tomar decisões acertadas quando o assunto é telefonia móvel. Portanto, este guia vai te deixar tudo o que você precisa saber. Continue aqui! Operadoras de telefonia móvel no Brasil Agora que já entendemos a importância da telefonia móvel para as empresas, é hora de conhecer as operadoras que atuam no Brasil e suas particularidades. Vem com a gente! 1.1. Principais operadoras e suas áreas de atuação O mercado brasileiro de telefonia móvel é dominado por algumas grandes operadoras, que possuem ampla cobertura e oferecem diversos serviços voltados ao público empresarial. As principais operadoras são: Vivo Líder de mercado, a Vivo possui a maior cobertura no país, atendendo a praticamente todas as regiões. A operadora oferece uma gama variada de planos empresariais e tem foco na qualidade e velocidade de sua rede. Claro Com presença significativa em todo o território nacional, a Claro também oferece diversos planos e serviços para empresas. A operadora se destaca por investir em tecnologias inovadoras, como a rede 5G. TIM Com uma cobertura abrangente, especialmente nas áreas urbanas, a TIM busca oferecer planos empresariais competitivos e com boa relação custo-benefício. A empresa também investe em tecnologia e inovação. Oi Presente em várias regiões do Brasil, a Oi tem como diferencial a oferta de planos empresariais integrados com serviços de telefonia fixa, internet e TV por assinatura. Algar Telecom Com atuação mais regionalizada, a Algar Telecom tem presença marcante no interior de alguns estados, como Minas Gerais e São Paulo. A empresa oferece soluções customizadas para atender às necessidades específicas das empresas de sua área de atuação. Com a Salvy ao seu lado, você pode ter a certeza de que sua empresa está em boas mãos quando se trata de telefonia móvel. 1.2. Vantagens e desvantagens das operadoras do mercado Escolher a operadora ideal para sua empresa pode ser uma tarefa complicada, mas a Salvy está aqui para ajudar! Vamos analisar as vantagens e desvantagens das principais operadoras: Possíveis vantagens das operadoras comuns: Planos diversificados e investimento em inovação. Maior cobertura, planos com bom custo-benefício e boa qualidade de sinal. Investimento em tecnologia e inovação, planos competitivos e boa cobertura. Oferta de planos integrados com outros serviços de telecomunicações. Soluções customizadas e atendimento próximo ao cliente. A cobertura pode ser menor em algumas áreas rurais e remotas. Menor cobertura em comparação às líderes de mercado e situação financeira instável da empresa. Agora é hora de explorar os planos empresariais e descobrir qual deles se encaixa perfeitamente no seu negócio. Vamos juntos continuar nossa jornada? 2.1. Tipos de planos e suas características As operadoras têm uma variedade de planos pensados especialmente para empresas, com diversas opções de serviços e preços. Confira algumas das categorias mais comuns: Planos corporativos (Enterprise) Ideais para empresas de médio e grande porte, que precisam de várias linhas e recursos específicos. Normalmente, incluem pacotes de minutos, SMS e internet, além de serviços extras, como chamadas em grupo e roaming. Planos PME (Pequenas e Médias Empresas) Criados para atender pequenas e médias empresas, esses planos trazem pacotes de serviços mais compactos e com preços mais em conta. Contam com minutos, SMS e internet, além de funcionalidades como ligações ilimitadas entre usuários da mesma operadora. Planos controle Com uma franquia fixa de serviços (minutos, SMS e internet), esses planos são perfeitos para empresas que desejam controlar melhor os gastos e têm um número menor de colaboradores. Planos pré-pagos Funcionam com a compra de créditos que são convertidos em serviços de telefonia e internet. São indicados para empresas que buscam flexibilidade e têm demandas variáveis ou sazonais. Porém, não é muito praticado pelas principais operadoras em plano para empresas, mas você pode vincular um CPF e fazer como pessoa física. 2.2. Comparativo de preços e serviços entre operadoras Para escolher um plano empresarial, é crucial comparar os preços e serviços das diferentes operadoras. Veja algumas dicas para facilitar essa comparação são: Identifique as necessidades da sua empresa: Defina o número de linhas, quantidade de minutos, SMS e internet necessários para o funcionamento do seu negócio. Pesquise os planos disponíveis: Acesse os sites das operadoras, entre em contato com os representantes comerciais e solicite orçamentos. Compare os serviços e preços: Verifique quais planos oferecem os recursos que sua empresa precisa e analise os custos envolvidos. Leve em conta a qualidade do sinal e a cobertura: Avalie a qualidade do sinal e a abrangência da cobertura das operadoras em sua região. 2.3. Como escolher o plano ideal para sua empresa Com todas essas informações em mãos, é hora de escolher o plano perfeito para sua empresa. Separamos algumas dicas para te ajudar nessa decisão: Considere o perfil da sua empresa: Pense no tamanho do seu negócio, no número de funcionários que utilizarão os serviços e nas suas necessidades específicas de comunicação. Estabeleça um orçamento: Determine quanto sua empresa pode investir em telefonia móvel e busque planos que se encaixem nesse valor. Compare os planos e operadoras: Utilize as informações que coletou para comparar os diferentes planos e operadoras, levando em consideração os serviços oferecidos, os preços e a qualidade do sinal. Não tenha medo de negociar: Entre em contato com as operadoras e tente negociar melhores condições, como descontos, pacotes adicionais ou serviços exclusivos. Teste e avalie: Após escolher o plano e a operadora, monitore o desempenho dos serviços e verifique se eles estão atendendo às expectativas e necessidades do seu negócio. Caso necessário, não hesite em reavaliar e ajustar suas escolhas. Tecnologias e infraestrutura de telefonia móvel Entender as tecnologias e a infraestrutura de telefonia móvel é crucial para aproveitar ao máximo os recursos oferecidos pelos planos empresariais. Vamos mergulhar nesse universo juntos? 3.1. Evolução da tecnologia: do 2G ao 5G A telefonia móvel evoluiu bastante ao longo dos anos, passando por várias gerações, cada uma trazendo avanços significativos em termos de velocidade, capacidade e qualidade: 2G : A segunda geração trouxe a comunicação digital, permitindo o envio de SMS e a transmissão de dados em baixa velocidade. 3G : A terceira geração proporcionou uma revolução na internet móvel, com velocidades maiores e melhor qualidade de conexão. Permitiu o uso de aplicativos e a navegação na web de forma mais eficiente. 4G : A quarta geração aumentou significativamente a velocidade da internet móvel, possibilitando o streaming de vídeos em alta qualidade, videoconferências e a utilização de aplicativos mais complexos. 5G : A quinta geração, que está em processo de implantação no Brasil, promete velocidades ainda maiores, latência extremamente baixa e maior capacidade de conexões simultâneas, abrindo caminho para inovações como a Internet das Coisas (IoT) e a comunicação entre máquinas. 3.2. Cobertura e qualidade do sinal no Brasil A cobertura e a qualidade do sinal de telefonia móvel no Brasil variam de acordo com a operadora e a região. Nas áreas urbanas, a cobertura geralmente é mais ampla e a qualidade do sinal mais consistente. Porém, em áreas rurais e remotas, a cobertura pode ser limitada e a qualidade do sinal menos confiável. Dessa forma, antes de escolher uma operadora, é importante verificar a cobertura e a qualidade do sinal em sua região e nas áreas em que sua empresa atua. 3.3. A importância da internet móvel nas empresas A internet móvel se tornou um recurso indispensável para as empresas, pois permite a comunicação e a troca de informações em tempo real, independentemente da localização dos colaboradores. Além disso, a internet móvel possibilita o uso de aplicativos e sistemas em nuvem, facilitando a gestão e a colaboração entre equipes. A escolha do plano de telefonia móvel adequado deve levar em consideração a importância da internet móvel para o seu negócio, garantindo velocidade e estabilidade para o uso dos recursos necessários. Com o conhecimento das tecnologias e da infraestrutura de telefonia móvel, sua empresa estará preparada para tomar decisões informadas e aproveitar ao máximo os benefícios da comunicação móvel. Vamos agora continuar aprendendo um pouco mais sobre os aparelhos ideais para sua empresa? Aparelhos e dispositivos móveis para empresas Além de escolher o plano e a operadora ideais, é fundamental selecionar os aparelhos e dispositivos móveis que atendam às necessidades da sua empresa. Vamos explorar esse tema juntos? 4.1. Principais marcas e modelos de smartphones O mercado de smartphones é vasto e conta com diversas marcas e modelos. Algumas das principais marcas disponíveis no Brasil são: Apple A gigante da tecnologia oferece modelos de iPhone com excelente desempenho, design elegante e recursos avançados, como o sistema operacional iOS e a integração com outros dispositivos da marca. Samsung Líder no mercado de smartphones Android, a Samsung possui uma ampla gama de modelos, desde opções mais acessíveis até dispositivos topo de linha, como a série Galaxy S e Note. Motorola A Motorola é conhecida por oferecer smartphones com bom custo-benefício e recursos interessantes, como a linha Moto G e Moto Z. Xiaomi A marca chinesa vem ganhando espaço no mercado brasileiro com smartphones de ótimo desempenho e preços competitivos, como os modelos da série Redmi e Mi. 4.2. Como escolher o smartphone ideal para sua empresa Agora, para escolher o smartphone perfeito para sua empresa, considere os seguintes aspectos: Necessidades do seu negócio: Pense nas funcionalidades que seus colaboradores precisam, como câmera, espaço de armazenamento, processador e bateria. Sistema operacional: Verifique se a sua empresa tem preferência por iOS ou Android, levando em conta a compatibilidade com aplicativos e sistemas utilizados. Custo-benefício: Avalie o orçamento disponível e busque aparelhos que ofereçam as melhores especificações pelo preço que sua empresa pode pagar. Durabilidade e resistência: Opte por smartphones com boa reputação em relação à durabilidade e resistência, especialmente se os dispositivos forem utilizados em ambientes mais exigentes. Suporte e garantia: Escolha marcas que ofereçam bom suporte ao cliente e garantias adequadas. 4.3. Uso de tablets e outros dispositivos móveis no ambiente corporativo Além dos smartphones, outros dispositivos móveis, como tablets, smartwatches e notebooks, também podem ser úteis no ambiente corporativo. Esses dispositivos podem ser empregados para: Apresentações e reuniões: Tablets e notebooks são excelentes ferramentas para apresentações e reuniões, permitindo acesso rápido a informações e recursos visuais. Trabalho remoto e mobilidade: Tablets e notebooks proporcionam maior flexibilidade e mobilidade para colaboradores que trabalham fora do escritório. Monitoramento e controle: Smartwatches podem ser utilizados para monitorar atividades e alertas importantes, além de controlar dispositivos IoT e sistemas automatizados. Pense um pouco: ao considerar os aparelhos e dispositivos móveis adequados para sua empresa, você garantirá maior eficiência e produtividade no trabalho. Então, agora que você conhece um pouco mais sobre os dispositivos mais comuns para empresas, qual seria sua escolha? Aplicativos e soluções móveis para empresas Com os dispositivos e planos de telefonia móvel certos, é hora de explorar os aplicativos e soluções que podem ajudar sua empresa a maximizar a produtividade e a comunicação. Vamos conferir algumas opções interessantes? 5.1. Aplicativos de comunicação e produtividade Existem diversos aplicativos que podem facilitar a comunicação e a colaboração entre os colaboradores da sua empresa. Alguns exemplos incluem: WhatsApp Business: Versão empresarial do popular aplicativo de mensagens, que permite a comunicação rápida e eficiente entre colaboradores e clientes. Slack : Plataforma de comunicação e colaboração que integra mensagens, chamadas e videoconferências, além de permitir a conexão com outros aplicativos e serviços. Trello : Ferramenta de gerenciamento de projetos baseada em cartões e quadros, que ajuda a organizar tarefas e acompanhar o progresso do trabalho. Google Workspace : Pacote de aplicativos do Google que inclui Gmail, Google Drive, Google Agenda, Google Meet e outros, facilitando a colaboração e o compartilhamento de informações. 5.2. Soluções de gestão e monitoramento de dispositivos móveis Gerenciar e monitorar os dispositivos móveis utilizados pelos colaboradores da empresa é fundamental para garantir a segurança das informações e o uso adequado dos recursos. Geralmente, você não vai precisar se aprofundar muito sobre esses sistemas. Afinal, a própria operadora pode te oferecer uma interface para gerenciamento. Contudo, vale a pena ficar ligado sobre como eles funcionam e suas diferenças: Mobile Device Management (MDM): Permite o gerenciamento centralizado dos dispositivos móveis, incluindo configurações, atualizações, políticas de segurança e controle de acesso. Mobile Application Management (MAM) : Foca no gerenciamento de aplicativos nos dispositivos móveis, permitindo a instalação, atualização e remoção de apps de forma centralizada. Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM): Combina as funcionalidades do MDM e do MAM, oferecendo uma solução completa para o gerenciamento de dispositivos móveis e aplicativos no ambiente corporativo. 5.3. Integração da telefonia móvel com sistemas de telefonia fixo e VoIP Muito bem! Você está ficando craque em telefonia móvel. E talvez você já possua sistemas que existam na empresa, por exemplo, telefonia fixa e VoIP. A integração da telefonia móvel com sistemas de telefonia fixo e VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) pode melhorar ainda mais a comunicação e a colaboração na sua empresa. Veja algumas vantagens dessa integração: Ramais móveis: Permite a utilização de ramais móveis, conectando os colaboradores à rede de telefonia da empresa, mesmo estando fora do escritório. Encaminhamento de chamadas: Facilita o encaminhamento de chamadas entre telefones fixos e móveis, garantindo que os colaboradores estejam sempre acessíveis. Redução de custos: A integração entre telefonia móvel e VoIP pode resultar em economia de custos, especialmente em chamadas internacionais e de longa distância. Portanto, com o uso de aplicativos e soluções adequadas, sua empresa estará pronta para enfrentar os desafios do mundo moderno e aproveitar ao máximo os benefícios da telefonia móvel. Segurança e privacidade na telefonia móvel empresarial A segurança e a privacidade dos dados são aspectos cruciais na telefonia móvel empresarial. Logo, é fundamental estar ciente dos riscos e adotar medidas para proteger as informações da sua empresa. Vamos abordar alguns pontos importantes sobre esse tema. 6.1. Riscos e vulnerabilidades em dispositivos móveis Dispositivos móveis podem estar expostos a diversas ameaças, como: Malware : Softwares maliciosos que podem comprometer a segurança e o funcionamento dos dispositivos. Ataques de phishing : Tentativas de obter informações confidenciais por meio de mensagens ou aplicativos falsos. Roubo ou perda de dispositivos: A perda ou o roubo de smartphones e tablets pode resultar no acesso não autorizado a dados corporativos. Uso inadequado de aplicativos: A instalação e o uso de aplicativos não seguros podem expor os dispositivos a riscos e vulnerabilidades. 6.2. Políticas de segurança e uso responsável Para garantir a segurança e a privacidade na telefonia móvel empresarial, é essencial estabelecer políticas claras de uso responsável e segurança, que incluam: Uso de senhas e autenticação : Implementação de senhas fortes e mecanismos de autenticação, como a biometria, para proteger os dispositivos e os dados. Atualizações e patches de segurança: Manutenção dos dispositivos e aplicativos sempre atualizados, aplicando patches de segurança quando necessário. Controle de acesso a aplicativos e serviços: Restringir o acesso a aplicativos e serviços não autorizados e garantir que apenas aplicativos confiáveis sejam utilizados. Treinamento e conscientização dos colaboradores: Oferecer treinamentos e orientações sobre as melhores práticas de segurança e uso responsável dos dispositivos móveis. 6.3. Soluções de proteção e recuperação de dados Além das políticas de segurança e uso responsável, é importante contar com soluções que protejam e recuperem os dados em caso de incidentes, como: Software antivírus e antimalware: Utilização de soluções de segurança para prevenir e detectar ameaças em tempo real. Criptografia de dados: Proteção dos dados armazenados e transmitidos por meio de criptografia, garantindo que apenas pessoas autorizadas possam acessá-los. Backup e recuperação: Implementação de soluções de backup e recuperação de dados para garantir a continuidade dos negócios em caso de perda ou comprometimento das informações. Mas, por que isso é importante? Porque ao abordar a segurança e a privacidade na telefonia móvel empresarial de maneira abrangente e proativa, você protegerá os dados da sua empresa e garantirá a tranquilidade de todos os envolvidos. Tendências e inovações em telefonia móvel para empresas O mundo da telefonia móvel está em constante evolução, e as empresas precisam estar por dentro das últimas tendências e inovações para se manterem competitivas. Vamos dar uma olhada em algumas dessas novidades e como elas podem impactar o ambiente empresarial? 7.1. Internet das Coisas (IoT) e sua aplicação no ambiente empresarial A Internet das Coisas (IoT) está revolucionando a forma como os dispositivos se conectam e interagem, criando uma rede de objetos inteligentes que podem coletar e compartilhar dados. No ambiente empresarial, a IoT pode: Otimizar processos : Sensores e dispositivos conectados podem monitorar e automatizar processos, melhorando a eficiência e reduzindo custos. Melhorar a tomada de decisões: A coleta e análise de dados em tempo real podem ajudar na tomada de decisões mais assertivas e baseadas em informações concretas. Criar novos modelos de negócios : A IoT permite o desenvolvimento de produtos e serviços inovadores, abrindo novas oportunidades de negócios. 7.2. Inteligência Artificial (IA) e automação na comunicação móvel A Inteligência Artificial (IA) e a automação estão transformando a comunicação móvel, oferecendo recursos como: Assistente virtual : Os assistentes virtuais, como o Google Assistant e a Siri, podem auxiliar os colaboradores na realização de tarefas e na busca de informações, aumentando a produtividade. Chatbots : Os chatbots podem ser usados para automatizar o atendimento ao cliente e a comunicação interna, agilizando processos e melhorando a experiência do usuário. Análise preditiva : A IA pode ajudar a identificar tendências e padrões nos dados, permitindo uma melhor tomada de decisões e previsão de resultados. 7.3. Futuro da telefonia móvel e impacto no mundo dos negócios As inovações em telefonia móvel continuarão a evoluir, trazendo impactos significativos para o mundo dos negócios. Confira algumas tendências futuras: Redes 5G e além: A implementação de redes 5G trará maior velocidade e capacidade, possibilitando novas aplicações e melhorando a conectividade entre dispositivos. Realidade Aumentada (AR) e Realidade Virtual (VR) : A integração de tecnologias de AR e VR na telefonia móvel pode transformar a forma como os colaboradores interagem e aprendem, oferecendo experiências imersivas e inovadoras. Convergência de tecnologias: A fusão de tecnologias, como IoT, IA, blockchain e telefonia móvel, criará novas oportunidades e desafios para as empresas. Portanto, fique sempre de olho nas tendências e inovações do mercado para garantir que sua empresa esteja preparada para enfrentar os desafios do futuro. Dicas para otimizar a gestão da telefonia móvel na empresa Estamos chegando ao fim do nosso Guia Completo da Telefonia Móvel. Agora, vamos conferir algumas dicas de otimização na gestão de telefonia móvel da sua empresa. Gerenciar a telefonia móvel de forma eficiente é fundamental para garantir a satisfação dos colaboradores e o melhor aproveitamento dos recursos disponíveis. Separamos algumas dicas para ajudá-lo nessa tarefa: 8.1. Monitoramento e controle de gastos com telefonia Manter os gastos com telefonia sob controle é essencial para a saúde financeira da empresa. Veja algumas ações que podem ser tomadas: Estabelecer limites de gastos: Definir limites para gastos com telefonia, como minutos de chamadas, mensagens e uso de dados, e acompanhar o consumo regularmente. Analisar detalhadamente as faturas : Verificar as faturas mensais em busca de possíveis erros ou cobranças indevidas. Negociar com as operadoras: Manter contato com as operadoras para negociar melhores condições e descontos nos planos empresariais. Você consegue identificar qual dessas ações você pode implementar hoje? 8.2. Treinamento e suporte aos colaboradores Oferecer treinamento e suporte adequados aos colaboradores é fundamental para garantir o uso correto e eficiente dos dispositivos móveis e serviços de telefonia: Capacitar os colaboradores: Promover treinamentos sobre o uso dos dispositivos, aplicativos e políticas de segurança. Estabelecer canais de suporte: Disponibilizar canais de comunicação para que os colaboradores possam tirar dúvidas e solicitar suporte quando necessário. Incentivar o uso responsável: Incentivar os colaboradores a utilizar os dispositivos e serviços de telefonia de maneira responsável e consciente. 8.3. Revisão e atualização periódica dos planos e dispositivos Revisar e atualizar os planos e dispositivos periodicamente é importante para garantir que a empresa esteja sempre utilizando as melhores soluções disponíveis: Avaliar os planos e serviços: Verificar regularmente se os planos e serviços contratados ainda atendem às necessidades da empresa e se estão alinhados com as últimas tendências do mercado. body_text: Jeep® is one of the most recognizable brands in the world. Its vehicles, such as the Wrangler, are icons in automotive history. For the past 30 years, Mark Allen has shepherded exterior design for the Jeep brand, first as a designer and working his way up to vice president of Jeep design. Throughout those decades, Allen ensured the brand stayed true to its iconic design heritage, while evolving and moving forward. Now, Allen begins a new chapter as he retires from the Stellantis Product Design Office at the end of this month. From Car Designer to Jeep Enthusiast Even at the age of 5, Allen knew he wanted to be an automotive designer. While studying at the College for Creative Studies in Detroit, Allen knew he wanted to work for the Chrysler Corporation and specifically for Tom Gale, the then head of design. Why? Allen says Gale’s design team was turning out some incredible concepts and there was just an energy about them. Allen landed an internship in 1993, making his dream to work with Gale come true. His excitement over being hired in 1994 after graduating from CCS was tempered because the job was in the Jeep Truck design studio. “I wanted to be a car designer; Jeep was all about trucks,” says Allen. That changed in 2003 when Allen attended his first Easter Jeep Safari in Moab, Utah. “The whole vibe of the event really turned the corner for me, and I became a super Jeep enthusiast,” he says. “I had never driven off-road like that before. I was rock-crawling and appreciated the technique and finesse needed. I fell in love.” Allen came home and immediately bought his first Jeep Wrangler, a 2001 TJ. He still owns it. The Road to Easter Jeep Safari Before Moab, there was the SkunkWerks. Allen worked in and eventually led this team of in-house enthusiasts — designers, engineers, marketers, and product planners — that created and built one-off custom vehicles. The team was renamed (Mopar) Underground in deference to Lockheed Martin’s ownership of Skunk Works. The Underground team focused on building vehicles for the annual Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) show in Las Vegas. Allen’s team built the 2004 Jeep KJ “Liberator” Liberty concept specifically for SEMA. Allen knew it was the type of vehicle that should be at the Easter Jeep Safari, so he took it there, marking the brand’s first appearance at the annual event. Since then, the brand has used the Easter Jeep Safari to showcase new concept vehicles and interact with Jeep enthusiasts, learning how they use their vehicles, what they like and what they want to see on Jeep vehicles. The Easter Jeep Safari is now a rite of passage for all Jeep brand designers. Allen’s team has created numerous concept vehicles for Easter Jeep Safari. Out of all of them, his favorite is the Jeep Nukizer 715 , an all-purpose truck that pays homage to the beloved, military-only Kaiser M-715 truck. Allen sketched the concept and managed the entire build process. “If I could take one home with me, this would be it,” he says with a smile. Jeep Vehicle Legacy When Allen started 30 years ago, the brand had three products and a small design studio. Today, the Jeep vehicle lineup comprises the Cherokee, Compass, Gladiator, Grand Cherokee, three-row Grand Cherokee L, Grand Cherokee 4xe, Renegade, Wrangler and Wrangler 4xe. Allen also oversaw the return of the Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer as a premium extension of the Jeep brand. Allen’s favorite vehicles are the 2018 (JL) Wrangler and the 2020 (JT) Gladiator. He credits former CEO Sergio Marchionne for championing the Jeep Gladiator, the brand’s first pickup truck since the Comanche, which was discontinued in 1992. Keeping Easter Eggs Quiet The first Easter Egg was hatched on the 2011 Jeep Grand Cherokee, when a Jeep designer created a tiny Wrangler front end icon featuring the grille and headlamps, with the intention of it being placed in the middle of the headlamps. “There was never a plan (for Easter Eggs). We do it for our customers because we want them to know that their vehicle was created by an actual person who is passionate about the brand,” Allen says. “The secret is not to overdo it, not do too many and be too obvious.” Allen says he doesn’t know how many Easter Eggs have been created, nor do they keep track of them. Finding them? Allen and the Jeep design team have taken an oath of secrecy: “These are for our customers, and I love how thrilled they are when they find them.” His personal favorite “eggs” are the spider on the Jeep Renegade, a project that paired the U.S. and Italian design teams, and the 419 on the Jeep Gladiator — which pays respect to the men and women who work at the Toledo Assembly Complex. Riding the Wave Reflecting on his 30 years, Allen says he is most proud of the growth of the Jeep brand, the proliferation of models and the brand’s global success. He has enjoyed being at the helm and keeping the design philosophy intact while modernizing it. “It’s super fun for us as designers to work on these vehicles, to put the effort, care and love into them and then show them to people. It’s very rewarding,” he says. Allen looks forward to the continued evolution of the Jeep brand and what the future has to offer, particularly the introduction of the Jeep Recon EV. How does Allen want to be remembered? “That I didn’t screw it up,” he says with a laugh. “Mark has left his mark not only on the Jeep brand, but his influence on the designers that have had the pleasure of working with him. They will never forget his coaching style, whether it’s negotiating with engineering or sweating the details on every millimeter of our beloved Jeep vehicles,” said Chief Design Officer, Ralph Gilles. “I hope that when he looks back on his career, he feels the way we do, which is gratification for the legacy he helped to create that will be enjoyed by the world for years to come.” Chief Design Officer, Ralph Gilles So, what’s next? Allen and his wife, Andrea, plan to spend the next few months traveling and seeing family and friends. “We’re shopping for a new town, too. We drew a line along the Continental Divide, and we’re headed left of that.” Safe travels to you, my friend. Thank you for your dedication to the Jeep brand and community. Jeep Dianna Gutierrez Read More

title: Breaking For Summer: Keep Cool With These New Features

body_text: The end of the school year is upon us, but the excitement at CodeCombat is just getting started! Join us as we look through our latest product update, jam-packed with brand-new features and improvements. And that's not all! Our Changelog is your one-stop shop to stay up-to-date on all the latest and greatest features. So, what are you waiting for? Let's dive in and discover what's new at CodeCombat! High-Contrast Color Scheme for Enhanced Accessibility As part of our ongoing mission, we believe everyone should have the opportunity to learn and excel at coding, regardless of their abilities. That's why we're proud to introduce our latest feature - a colorblind-friendly syntax highlighting color scheme, now available in both Ozaria and CodeCombat. Our high-contrast color scheme was crafted with low-vision and colorblind players in mind, ensuring that everyone can easily read and understand code. We've also made further enhancements by adding a lighter background to the code editor, providing even more contrast. Additionally, we've highlighted a few more types of code, making it easier to code like a pro. Advanced Level Control for Teachers In the Teacher Dashboard, teachers now have the power to individually lock, skip, or make certain levels optional for their students. This level control feature enables teachers to tailor their students' learning journeys to fit their unique needs and abilities. In addition, with the option to set lock dates for specific levels, teachers can also schedule lessons and assignments with greater flexibility and precision. Increased Teacher Usability With Test as Student Feature Our Test as Student feature allows teachers to view CodeCombat's games through the eyes of a student. With just a few clicks, teachers can switch to an automatic student account, simplifying the process of testing code, saving progress, and allowing teachers to see firsthand how their students navigate challenges and identify potential improvement areas. To access the Test as Student feature, navigate to " My Account " in the navigation bar and select " Test as Student. " This feature is available for all teachers on both Ozaria and CodeCombat platforms, and we hope that it will enhance the teaching experience and help students succeed in their coding journey. Revamped CodeCombat Game Design Lessons & Slides! We're excited to announce the latest update to our CodeCombat Game Design curriculum! We've updated the lesson plans and slides for Game Design 1 and 2 , ensuring they work seamlessly together. You can now access this new and improved curriculum in the Course Guide and Teacher Toolkit . But that's not all - we've also created all-new lesson plans and slides for Game Design 3! These updated materials offer students a more engaging and comprehensive learning experience and are available in the Course Guide and Teacher Toolkit . Our team is continually working to improve our curriculums, and we're already hard at work updating the Web Development curriculum. So stay tuned for another exciting announcement soon! AI League Esports Curriculum in CodeCombat Teacher Toolkit We have added AI League Esports lesson slides in the CodeCombat Teacher Toolkit for easier access. This curriculum equips teachers with the resources they need to bring the world of competitive coding into their classrooms, enabling students to develop essential skills in strategy and problem-solving. With the AI League Esports curriculum, teachers can help students take their coding skills to the next level while having fun and enjoying the competitive spirit of esports. Spanish Subtitles For Ozaria Cutscenes Spanish subtitles have been added to all Ozaria cutscene videos. These subtitles are enabled by default for users who have selected Spanish as their preferred interface language. This update makes Ozaria more accessible to Spanish-speaking players and enhances their gaming experience. Now, players can fully immerse themselves in the game's storyline without language barriers. Convert Home Accounts to Student Accounts in Ozaria with Ease We've simplified the process of converting CodeCombat home accounts to Ozaria student accounts, so students who create accounts before receiving a classroom invite can quickly get started with coding in class. Previously, students could only convert their accounts to CodeCombat classroom accounts, but now they can easily convert to student accounts in Ozaria as well. Thanks to this, teachers can invite students to their Ozaria classrooms with peace of mind, knowing that the conversion process is straightforward and accessible. Higher Framerate Rendering for Improved Gameplay CodeCombat's games have always been rendered at 30 frames per second (FPS). While this may be acceptable for watching TV, it doesn't quite cut it for fast-paced coding game action. So, with the power of modern GPUs, we decided to take advantage of higher framerates for a smoother gaming experience. Starting now, our games will render at whatever the innate refresh rate of the player's device is, up to a maximum of 240 FPS. This means that players with capable devices can enjoy our games with a higher framerate, resulting in a smoother and more responsive gameplay experience. Say goodbye to choppy animations and lagging gameplay, and say hello to improved game performance with higher framerate rendering! CodeCombat API Upgrades for Improved Integration If you're a CodeCombat partner looking to integrate our platform into your coding education business, we have some exciting updates to share! Our API now includes the following resources to help you streamline the integration process: New API documentation Postman collection Node.js SDK ( Coming soon ) Java SDK We also encourage you to check out our partners page for more examples of how our partners are using the CodeCombat API to enhance their coding education offerings. Always Improving Thank you for joining us on this journey to review our latest features and improvements! As always, we welcome your questions and feedback. title: Future Fields Appoints SynBioBeta Founder John Cumbers to Advisory Board
body_text: EDMONTON, Alberta, Canada (May 10, 2023) – Future Fields, a pioneering biotechnology company that has built the world’s first synthetic biology system to use fruit flies for recombinant protein production, today announced that John Cumbers, Ph.D, the founder and CEO of SynBioBeta , has joined the company’s advisory board. Cumbers brings extensive experience in scientific innovation and is a leading advocate for the expanded use of synthetic biology to build a better, more sustainable planet. “We are pleased to welcome John Cumbers to the Future Fields advisory board at such an exciting time of growth for our company. John is a highly respected, entrepreneurial advocate for the bioeconomy and a passionate thought leader for innovation that aligns with our pioneering fruit fly platform,” said Matt Anderson-Baron, Co-Founder and CEO of Future Fields. “John’s strategic perspective, guidance and in-depth knowledge of synthetic biology will be invaluable as we leverage the power of our sustainable biomanufacturing platform, the EntoEngine , to fuel a new wave of discoveries and protein-based drug production.” As the head of SynBioBeta, the premier innovation network for biological engineers, innovators, entrepreneurs, and investors, Cumbers has established himself as a leading authority on synthetic biology. He conducts the annual SynBioBeta Conference, hosts the SynBioBeta Podcast, advises a variety of startups on innovation and strategies, and serves as an operating partner and investor at the tech investment fund Data Collective. Cumbers also writes for Forbes as a senior contributor. In addition, he has written a book, entitled What’s Your Bio Strategy , and he worked as a bioengineer at NASA earlier in his career. He earned his Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, and Biochemistry from Brown University. “Future Fields is a shining example of what is incredible about the innovation driving the bioeconomy. Using fruit flies as ‘factories’ for recombinant proteins is an ingenious approach to bringing more scalable and sustainable solutions to biomanufacturing,” said Cumbers. “I am honored to support the incredible Future Fields team and contribute to their mission to change how we do science for humanity and the planet.” Cumbers joins two other Future Fields advisors: Michael Houghton, Ph.D., and Andrew Simmonds, Ph.D. Dr. Houghton was the Canada Excellence Research Chair in Virology from 2010-2018 and is currently the Li Ka Shing Professor of Virology at the University of Alberta, where he is also the Director of the Li Ka Shing Applied Virology Institute. He was jointly named the 2020 Nobel Prize winner in Physiology or Medicine along with Harvey J. Alter and Charles M. Rice for their work in the discovery of the hepatitis C (HCV) virus. Dr. Simmonds is Department Chair and professor at the Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry – Cell Biology Department at the University of Alberta. He is a distinguished scientist with a prolific track record of published research papers. Future Fields is advancing a new biomanufacturing paradigm by harnessing fruit flies. With its biomanufacturing platform, EntoEngine™, the company is focused on making significant strides to increase the supply of recombinant proteins for biological drugs, shrink the cost of research and development, and diminish the carbon footprint of bioreactors, which are typically big steel tanks. Future Fields aims to help the biopharmaceutical industry reduce the carbon impact caused by traditional bioreactors and enhance sustainability through synthetic biology. In February 2023, Future Fields announced a new suite of human recombinant protein products created for biomedical research and biopharma by its patented EntoEngine™ platform. These proteins include: a protein for wound healing and bone graft additive, a hormone responsible for breast milk development, a hormone that facilitates muscle development and maintenance, an important reproductive biology hormone, and a key protein used in stem cell research with applications in traumatic spinal cord injury, stroke, and severe burns.
